IoT security is an important topic, that it is not yet solved, and that there is still a lot to be done.
IoT devices need to be secured by design, that they should be able to dynamically adapt to threats and that security should be a first-order design concern, not an afterthought.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) IoT security threats, vulnerabilities and attacks; (2) IoT security solutions and architectures; (3) IoT security policies, mechanisms and tools; (4) IoT security evaluation and certification; and (5) IoT security education and training.

the development of novel security and privacy mechanisms to protect IoT systems and their users.

the IoT security research community needs a common vision and roadmap to address the challenges of securing the IoT.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the security of the IoT requires new approaches, and that the IoT security challenges are so complex and pervasive that they will likely require a paradigm shift in how security is approached.

IoT security is a complex and challenging task that requires the collaboration of multiple stakeholders and a multidisciplinary approach, where researchers and industry work together to develop new technologies and standards that can be deployed in the IoT.

we have identified and discussed a number of IoT security challenges that are not yet fully understood or addressed, and we have proposed a set of research directions that we believe will be instrumental for securing the IoT.

a new security paradigm is needed to secure the IoT and that the security of IoT devices should be addressed at all stages of the design cycle, from the initial requirements to the final deployment.
the IoT is a unique opportunity to rethink the way we secure our digital world, and that the research challenges we identified can help the IoT community to build a more secure and trustworthy IoT.
